candidates.title: Hamster: Private Transformer Inference via Fully Homomorphic Encryption
candidates.venue: International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications
candidates.abstract: Large transformer-based models have achieved remarkable performance in natural language processing and related fields, yet they pose significant privacy risks when handling sensitive data. Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) offers a natural solution for private transformer inference: the client encrypts the input data, the server performs inference directly on ciphertexts, and the results remain encrypted until decrypted by the key holder. However, FHE struggles to efficiently support non-linear activation functions, and encrypted inference often incurs substantial performance overhead and degrades model accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose Hamster, an FHE-based private transformer inference system that protects both client and server privacy. Our contributions are twofold. First, Hamster introduces a comprehensive set of more efficient approximations for the costly nonlinear functions in transformer models, significantly reducing the performance overhead of homomorphic evaluation. Second, unlike some existing works that only support a limited set of nonlinear components, Hamster implements a complete end-to-end evaluation pipeline for private transformer inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate Hamster achieves an average inference time of approximately 12 minutes per token, with minimal loss in model accuracy. This performance outperforms BumbleBee (NDSS 2025) by 2.2× and NEXUS (NDSS 2025) by 1.2×, highlighting the effectiveness and practicality of our system.
candidates.reason: IEEE公式abstractに基づく。Hamsterは完全準同型暗号下でTransformerの非線形GELU/Softmax等を効率的に近似し、クライアント入力とサーバーモデルを秘匿したままend-to-end推論するシステム。トークンあたり平均約12分と依然高コストながら、BumbleBee比2.2倍、NEXUS比1.2倍の推論高速化を報告。プライバシー制約下のTransformer推論実行時間削減という直接的システム技術なのでaccept。ただし一般的なLLMサービング性能への外挿はしない。
